title: Coherent external cup and arbitrary coefficients with projective cohomology
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $X,Y$ algebraic spaces over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume their structure maps are flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated: flatness is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism], quasi-compactness after every affine scheme test on the target, and quasi-separatedness means that the relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Put $P=X\times_TY$, with projections $p_X,p_Y$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. On each small etale site use structure-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and cohomology $H^i(Z,M)$ defined by right derived global sections of the underlying additive sheaf. Suppose $H_X^i=H^i(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $H_Y^i=H^i(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ are finite projective $R$-modules (direct summands of finite free modules) for all $i\geq0$, and both families vanish for sufficiently large $i$. For any $R$-module $N$, without a flatness or finiteness assumption, write $N_Z=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_RN$ for $Z=X,Y,P$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every $n\geq0$, the canonical coefficient maps
$$\alpha_{Z,N}^n:H^n(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\otimes_RN\longrightarrow H^n(Z,N_Z)$$
are isomorphisms for $Z=X,Y,P$, and the external cup maps, built from the global cup product [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product], are isomorphisms
$$\kappa_N^n:\left(\bigoplus_{i+j=n}H_X^i\otimes_R H_Y^j\right)\otimes_RN\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(P,N_P),\qquad(a\otimes b)\otimes n\longmapsto(p_X^*a\smile p_Y^*b)\cdot n.$$
Here $c\cdot n$ means cup with the degree-zero section $1\otimes n$ of $N_P$, so these formulas specify the actual maps. The coefficient maps are natural for homomorphisms of $N$ and for all $T$-morphisms between spaces satisfying the stated hypotheses; these pullbacks preserve identities, compositions, units and cup products. The assertions commute with localization $R\to R_s$ and the corresponding base changes of the spaces and modules. Cup product is associative, unital, bilinear and graded commutative: $ba=(-1)^{ij}ab$ in degrees $i,j$. For $N=R$, $\kappa_R^*$ is an isomorphism of graded algebras when the source has multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=(-1)^{\deg(b)\deg(c)}ac\otimes bd$. All these statements use ordinary quasi-coherent structure-module coefficients, not constant finite etale coefficients.

source.place: Tags 08IN (lemma-cohomology-base-change, projection formula) and 08IR (lemma-compare-base-change, Tor-independent base change), for the algebraic-space coherent Kunneth construction; the finite-projective-cohomology specialization with arbitrary N and its naturality is agent-stated. Cup-product identities: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0FPL (lemma-cup-product-associative), 0FPM (lemma-cup-product-commutative), 0H9A (lemma-base-change-cup-product). This is the cohomology-level external-cup theorem, not a newly chosen decomposition of a derived object.

proof.text: Write $f:X\to T$, $g:Y\to T$, $h:P\to T$. The projections are base changes of $g,f$, respectively. Quasi-compactness is preserved by base change by the cited space lemma. Composites of quasi-compact maps are quasi-compact: testing on a quasi-compact target gives successively two quasi-compact inverse images. The diagonal of $P/T$ is the composite of the two base changes imposing equality of the $X$ and $Y$ coordinates; thus it is quasi-compact by the same argument. The same diagonal argument proves preservation of quasi-separatedness by base change. Flatness of the projections follows from base-change stability; flatness of $h$ follows on etale charts from composition of flat ring maps. Consequently $X,Y,P$ and their localizations satisfy the flat qcqs hypotheses needed below.

source.place: Tags 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact); the diagonal factorization is written out here; flatness on charts

proof.text: Put $C_Z=R\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ in $D(R)$. The ringed-site module/abelian comparison identifies $H^i(C_Z)$ canonically with the cohomology in the statement, including its scalar action. The existing derived external-cup theorem gives the actual isomorphism $k:C_X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C_Y\to C_P$, natural in $X,Y$, with its product, unit and base-change compatibilities. We use that theorem only in the derived form; neither ordinary tensor cohomology nor arbitrary-module coefficient comparison follows without the next steps.

source.place: Tags 08IN and 08IR, as assembled in lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-external-cup; module/abelian comparison in sites-cohomology.tex

proof.text: Here is the elementary splitting needed for $C_X$ and $C_Y$, and later for $C_P$. For any representative complex $L$ of an object $C$ whose cohomology is projective and zero outside finitely many degrees, the quotient $Z^i(L)\twoheadrightarrow H^i(L)$ has an $R$-linear section $s_i$ by the lifting definition of projectivity. Let $S_C^i=H^i(L)$ with zero differentials and define $S_C\to L$ in degree $i$ by $s_i$ followed by $Z^i(L)\hookrightarrow L^i$. It is a chain map and induces the identity on every cohomology module, hence becomes an isomorphism in the derived category. The complex $S_C$ is bounded; its terms are finite projective whenever the cohomology modules of $C$ are finite projective. Sections are used only to check invertibility, never to define a comparison map.

source.place: Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), lifting along Z^i(L) -> H^i(L); explicit agent argument with the derived-category definition

proof.text: Each $S_C$ is K-flat: its terms are flat because projective modules are flat, and the bounded-above-flat criterion applies. A K-flat first factor computes derived tensor with an arbitrary complex. Thus the canonical cocycle tensor map $\bigoplus_{i+j=n}H^i(C_X)\otimes_RH^j(C_Y)\to H^n(C_X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C_Y)$ is an isomorphism: on the models $S_{C_X},S_{C_Y}$ the total differential is zero and the degree-$n$ term is exactly that direct sum. It is the canonical map because the chosen sections induce the identity on cohomology and send $a\otimes b$ to the tensor of cycle representatives. Composing with $H^n(k)$ gives precisely $\kappa_R^n$ by the definition of the external cup. Each tensor of two finite projectives is a summand of a finite free module: tensor their finite-free retractions; finite direct sums preserve these retractions. Hence $H^n(C_P)$ is finite projective and vanishes above the sum of the two cohomological bounds.

source.place: K-flat tensor computation; Tag 0B6C (remark-cup-product), canonical cocycle pairing; finite-free retract calculation written here

proof.text: Apply the flat affine-base projection formula to each $Z=X,Y,P$, with $E=\mathcal O_Z[0]$ and the given arbitrary module $N$. The geometry was checked in Step 1. It gives the canonical natural isomorphism $\pi_{Z,N}:C_Z\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0]\to R\Gamma(Z,N_Z[0])$. Flatness over $R$ ensures that derived pullback of $N[0]$ is the ordinary quasi-coherent sheaf $N_Z[0]$; no flatness of $N$ is used. By Step 4 the cohomology of $C_P$, as well as that of $C_X,C_Y$, has the hypotheses of Step 3.

The canonical map $e_{Z,N}^n:H^n(C_Z)\otimes_RN\to H^n(C_Z\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0])$ is an isomorphism: compute it on $S_{C_Z}\otimes_RN[0]$, whose differential is zero and whose degree-$n$ term is $H^n(C_Z)\otimes_RN$. The source is K-flat, so this computation allows arbitrary $N$. The composite $H^n(\pi_{Z,N})e_{Z,N}^n$ is the specified $\alpha_{Z,N}^n$. Indeed, let $u_n:R\to N$ send $1$ to $n$. Naturality of the projection arrow in $u_n$ and its unit normalization show that on $a\otimes n$ this composite is $H^n(\mathcal O_Z\to N_Z)(a)$, where $1\mapsto1\otimes n$. The tensor-of-counits definition of cup with that degree-zero section gives exactly the same map: its adjoint is the counit tensored with the pulled-back section, and the unit triangle cancels the extra unit/counit. Thus this is $a\smile(1\otimes n)$, and all three coefficient maps are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0B6C (remark-cup-product) and the projection adjoint of Tag 0B56; explicit unit/counit and cocycle computation

proof.text: Now $\kappa_N^n$ factors as $\left(\bigoplus_{i+j=n}H_X^i\otimes_RH_Y^j\right)\otimes_RN\xrightarrow{\kappa_R^n\otimes1}H^n(C_P)\otimes_RN\xrightarrow{\alpha_{P,N}^n}H^n(P,N_P)$. Both arrows are isomorphisms: a functor sends an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse maps, so tensoring the first with $N$ needs no exactness assumption. On each generator $(a\otimes b)\otimes n$, the displayed factorization sends it to $(p_X^*a\smile p_Y^*b)\smile(1\otimes n)$, exactly the formula in the statement.

source.place: Finite-projective specialization of Tags 08IN and 08IR; assembly from Steps 4 and 6

proof.text: For a module homomorphism $v:N\to N'$ the sheaf maps satisfy $(1\otimes v)u_n=u_{v(n)}$. For a $T$-morphism $t:Z'\to Z$, the coefficient pullback square for $u_n$ commutes, since both maps send a local section $a$ to $t^\sharp(a)\otimes n$. Naturality of the adjunction unit makes the induced cohomology pullback commute with this square; the mate-pasting identity gives identity and composition for these pullbacks. The formula from Step 6, $\alpha_{Z,N}^n(a\otimes n)=H^n(u_n)(a)$, therefore proves the claimed naturality in both variables. Cup products and units for structure coefficients, and naturality of $\kappa_R$, are supplied by the derived external-cup theorem. Applying the same coefficient square on $P$ and the factorization in Step 7 proves naturality of $\kappa_N$. These arguments do not require the $T$-morphism $t$ to be flat.

source.place: Adjunction-unit naturality and mate pasting; coefficient-map computation written here; structure-cup functoriality from the derived external-cup theorem

proof.text: For localization put $B=R_s$. The derived external-cup theorem supplies the canonical product-compatible isomorphisms $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C_Z\to C_{Z_B}$, commuting with pullbacks and $k$. Localization is flat, so tensoring a complex with $B$ preserves its cycles, boundaries and their quotient; hence $H^n(C_{Z_B})=B\otimes_RH^n(C_Z)$. The localized modules are finite projective, since the original finite-free retractions remain retractions after tensoring. With $N_B=B\otimes_RN$, the canonical coefficient identification is $(N_Z)|_{Z_B}=\mathcal O_{Z_B}\otimes_BN_B$; it sends $1\otimes n$ to $1\otimes(1\otimes n)$. Consequently Step 6 identifies the localized $\alpha$ with the $B$-coefficient $\alpha$ on each pure tensor. The product compatibility of the derived base-change map does the same for $\kappa_R$, and Step 7 then does it for $\kappa_N$. This verifies the actual localization squares, including their maps, rather than just objectwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08IR (lemma-compare-base-change), product compatibility; localization flatness and explicit coefficient generators

proof.text: Finally apply the associative, unital, symmetric derived algebra structure supplied by the external-cup theorem. On cocycles in degrees $i,j$ the derived symmetry is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$, so the induced cup is graded commutative; bilinearity is part of the cup construction. In the product of $(p_X^*a\smile p_Y^*b)$ and $(p_X^*c\smile p_Y^*d)$, associativity and the single interchange of $p_Y^*b$ with $p_X^*c$ give $(-1)^{\deg(b)\deg(c)}p_X^*(ac)\smile p_Y^*(bd)$. Units are preserved by the same theorem. Since every $\kappa_R^n$ is already bijective, these identities prove that $\kappa_R^*$ is the stated isomorphism of graded algebras.
